# Lex

Bộ gõ Tiếng Việt dùng kiểu gõ Telex được tùy chỉnh phù hợp với cách dùng của tác giả.

Mục đích của chương trình là để hiểu rõ hơn về tính khả thi của cấu trúc chương trình hỗ trợ đa nền
tảng trong đó phần thuật toán chính sẽ được viết trong 1 thư viện dùng chung bằng Zig và chương
trình chính được viết bởi ngôn ngữ phù hợp với từng nền tảng. Ý tưởng này bắt nguồn từ cách lập
trình của
[Dropbox](https://oleb.net/blog/2014/05/how-dropbox-uses-cplusplus-cross-platform-development/) và
[Ghostty](https://mitchellh.com/writing/ghostty-and-useful-zig-patterns).

Lưu ý: Dropbox đã chuyển sang cách lập trình khác vì khó khăn trong lúc tích hợp thư viện, tuyển
người, đào tạo... Những khó khăn này không phải là vấn đề lớn khi tác giả là người duy nhất chịu
trách nhiệm cho toàn bộ chương trình.

## Chạy được trên hệ điều hành

- macOS 26.0 trở về sau.

## Chức năng

- [x] Nhập Tiếng Việt kiểu Telex với một số tùy chỉnh:
  - [x] Bỏ dấu kiểu cũ: _òa_, _úy_. Ví dụ: _hòa_, _thúy_.
  - [x] Không bỏ dấu nếu từ bắt đầu bằng phụ âm không phải Tiếng Việt: _f_, _j_, _w_, _z_.
  - [x] Dấu của nguyên âm, phụ âm `d` phải bỏ liền sau ký tự đó.
  - [x] Dấu của từ có thể bỏ ở cuối từ.
- [x] Bật / tắt nhập Tiếng Việt: `Ctrl + Opt + Space`.
- [x] Chỉ hiện biểu tượng trên thanh Menu của macOS.

- [ ] Phím tắt để xóa trạng thái gõ Tiếng Việt: `Ctrl (left)`.
- [x] Khóa bàn phím bằng lựa chọn trên thanh Menu hoặc tổ hợp phím: `Ctrl + Opt + Cmd + L`.

Lưu ý: chương trình được thiết lập mặc định theo những chức năng trên và không thể tùy chỉnh. Người
dùng có thể tắt chức năng _Khởi động khi đăng nhập_ trong menu (macOS 26): System Settings \>
General \> Login Items & Extensions \> Open at Login.

## Hướng dẫn cấp quyền _Accessibility_ cho Lex

Vì bộ gõ Tiếng Việt cần truy cập vào tín hiệu gõ phím của người dùng để bỏ dấu, Lex cần được cung
cấp quyền _Accessibility_ trước khi khởi động. Truy cập vào menu: System Settings \> Privacy &
Security \> Accessibility: thêm _Lex.app_ vào danh sách được cấp quyền.

Khởi động Lex sau khi đã cấp quyền.

## Tự biên dịch chương trình

Yêu cầu:

- macOS 26 hoặc mới hơn.
- Zig 0.16.0.
- Xcode 26 hoặc mới hơn.

Biên dịch liblex.a:

```
zig build-obj -target aarch64-macos.26.0 -O ReleaseFast src/lex.zig -femit-bin=liblex.o \
    && xcrun libtool -static -o liblex.a liblex.o
```

Bên dịch Lex:

```
mkdir -p macos/Lex.app/Contents/MacOS/
swiftc -parse-as-library -import-objc-header src/lex.h ./liblex.a macos/Lex.swift -o macos/Lex.app/Contents/MacOS/Lex
```

Review a proposed simplification in @macos/Lex.swift. Do not produce example code, pseudocode, code snippets, API call sequences formatted as code, or a patch. Respond only in prose and, if useful, a compact tradeoff table.

Context: The keyboard is guaranteed to be US ANSI. The selected macOS input source is guaranteed to be exactly ABC (QWERTY) or Dvorak, with no other cases. The keyboard-lock shortcut is logical Ctrl+Option+Command+L. RegisterEventHotKey requires a physical virtual keycode. The current current_keyboard_lock_key_code implementation obtains Unicode layout data and scans virtual keycodes 0..<128 with UCKeyTranslate until it finds lowercase l. On input-source-change notification, the app re-registers the hotkey if the resolved keycode changed. The event tap also retains the registered keycode so the lock shortcut can pass through while all other keys are blocked.

Proposed direction: replace generic layout translation and scanning with a closed mapping from selected input-source identity to the two known US ANSI keycodes: ABC logical L is the ANSI L position; Dvorak logical L is the ANSI P position. Preserve input-source-change observation, hotkey re-registration, stored-keycode event-tap pass-through, registration failure handling, and unknown-source failure rather than silently defaulting. Use the stable TIS input-source identifier, not localized names.

Evaluate: (1) whether this is the smallest sound design under the assumptions, (2) whether TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource versus TISCopyCurrentKeyboardInputSource is the right source of identity here, (3) any macOS identifier/keycode subtleties, races, or lifecycle issues that the approach must account for, and (4) exactly what existing complexity can be deleted versus retained. Output: recommendation, required corrections, retained/deleted responsibilities, and verification plan. Again, absolutely no example code or pseudocode.

run.result:
## Recommendation

Approve the simplification with two corrections: use TISCopyCurrentKeyboardInputSource for identity, and clear any stale registration when identity cannot be resolved. Under the stated closed assumptions, a direct two-case mapping is the smallest sound design and is materially clearer than retaining generic Unicode-layout translation.

The tradeoff is intentional: the implementation becomes coupled to Apple’s observed built-in source identifiers instead of supporting arbitrary layouts. That is appropriate only because ABC and standard Dvorak are guaranteed.

Scope: S, under one hour for implementation, plus manual macOS verification.

## Required corrections

1. **Use the selected input source, not the effective layout source.**

   TISCopyCurrentKeyboardInputSource is the semantically correct API because the decision is based on the identity of the selected source. Apple documents TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource as returning the underlying layout used for translation; when an input method is selected, that can be a different object from the selected source.

   Under the current ABC-or-Dvorak guarantee, both functions should return the same direct keyboard-layout source. Nevertheless, using the selected-source API preserves the exact contract and ensures a future input method backed by ABC or Dvorak fails as unknown rather than being silently accepted.

2. **Use the actual identifiers, with exact case-sensitive comparison.**

   The observed built-in identifiers are com.apple.keylayout.ABC and com.apple.keylayout.Dvorak. Do not derive them from display names, bundle identifiers, or Apple’s documented example naming pattern.

   Apple documents the input-source ID as a unique reverse-DNS identifier, but it does not publish these two literals as SDK constants or promise them as an immutable enumeration. Treat unknown identifiers as a supported failure path and verify the literals on the project’s minimum and current supported macOS versions.

3. **Use the named ANSI physical-position constants.**

   ABC maps to kVK_ANSI_L, whose value is 0x25. Standard Dvorak maps to kVK_ANSI_P, whose value is 0x23. These names identify physical US-ANSI positions, not the character currently produced there. Avoid unexplained numeric literals.

   This mapping does not cover Dvorak–QWERTY Command, other Dvorak variants, custom layouts, keyboard remappers, ISO/JIS hardware, or input methods. Those exclusions must remain genuine assumptions.

4. **Unknown-source failure must invalidate the old registration.**

   The current flow resolves the new keycode before unregistering the previous hotkey. Consequently, a resolution failure at [register_keyboard_lock_hot_key](macos/Lex.swift#L289-L305) leaves the previous physical key registered and retained for event-tap pass-through.

   That is not a clean unknown-source failure: after a source change, the stale physical chord may represent another logical key, may toggle the lock unexpectedly, and may pass through while the keyboard is locked. On an unknown identifier or unavailable identifier property, remove the old hotkey and clear the stored keycode while retaining the handler and observer so a later valid source change can recover. The menu remains the fallback for unlocking.

5. **Resolve identity inside the main-queue registration operation.**

   Preserve the current notification behavior of dispatching to the main queue and then querying the current source at execution time. Do not capture an identifier before dispatching; that would introduce stale registrations when source changes occur quickly.

## Retained and deleted responsibilities

### Retain

- One-time keyboard-lock event-handler installation and its termination cleanup.
- Input-source-change observation and observer removal, as implemented around [register_keyboard_lock_hot_key](macos/Lex.swift#L260-L287) and [unregister_keyboard_lock_hot_key](macos/Lex.swift#L325-L342).
- Main-queue serialization of notification handling at [keyboard_input_source_changed](macos/Lex.swift#L391-L396).
- The requirement that the event tap exist before the keyboard-lock hotkey is registered.
- The idempotence check that skips registration when the same keycode is already registered, while retrying if the hotkey reference is absent.
- Unregistration and state clearing before attempting a changed registration.
- Registration status checking and diagnostic reporting.
- Assignment of the hotkey reference and stored keycode only after successful registration.
- The registered-keycode accessor and exact-modifier event-tap pass-through at [registered_keyboard_lock_key_code](macos/Lex.swift#L608-L614) and [event_tap_callback](macos/Lex.swift#L738-L753).
- Copy ownership of the TIS input-source reference and safe extraction of the unretained input-source-ID property while that reference remains alive.
- Recovery after failure: the observer and Carbon event handler must remain installed even when resolution or registration fails.

### Delete

From [current_keyboard_lock_key_code](macos/Lex.swift#L344-L389), delete:

- Retrieval of Unicode keyboard-layout data.
- CFData-to-Data bridging for layout bytes.
- Unsafe byte binding to UCKeyboardLayout.
- The scan over virtual keycodes 0 through 127.
- Dead-key state, temporary character buffers, and character counts.
- UCKeyTranslate calls and their action, keyboard-type, and no-dead-key options.
- Translation-status and lowercase-L output matching.
- All failure branches that exist only for layout-data parsing or translation.

Retain the resolver itself as the single owner of source identity and physical-key selection. Carbon cannot be removed because the file still uses its hotkey, TIS, and virtual-key APIs extensively.

## Race and lifecycle assessment

The source-change notification and registration are not atomic with an external source switch. There can be a short interval in which the previous hotkey remains active or no hotkey is active during replacement. No additional synchronization is justified: each queued callback should query the latest selected source, so repeated notifications converge on current state.

The hotkey reference and retained keycode must continue to change together. Clearing the stored keycode before registration and setting it only after success prevents the event tap from passing a chord that Carbon did not successfully register.

The existing main-run-loop arrangement serializes registration with the event-tap callback. That assumption should remain explicit; moving either callback or registration to another queue would require synchronization around the hotkey reference, keycode, and lock state.

Observer installation and removal are currently balanced. No new cache, debounce mechanism, source object retention beyond resolution, or termination flag is warranted for this simplification.

## Verification plan

1. On every supported macOS baseline, confirm that selecting ABC reports com.apple.keylayout.ABC and selecting standard Dvorak reports com.apple.keylayout.Dvorak.
2. Under ABC, verify that logical Ctrl+Option+Command+L registers at the ANSI L position, toggles exactly once, and the ANSI P position does not trigger it.
3. Under Dvorak, verify that the same logical shortcut registers at the ANSI P position, toggles exactly once, and the ANSI L position does not trigger it.
4. Switch repeatedly between ABC and Dvorak while the application is running. Confirm that registration follows the final selected source and does not accumulate duplicate handlers or observers.
5. Switch sources while the keyboard is locked using an external or pointer-driven mechanism. Confirm that the newly mapped shortcut passes through and unlocks, while unrelated key events remain blocked.
6. Exercise an unsupported source despite the production guarantee. Confirm that no default mapping is selected, the previous registration and stored keycode are cleared, the unsupported physical chord is not passed through, a useful diagnostic is emitted, and switching back to ABC or Dvorak recovers automatically.
7. Force RegisterEventHotKey failure through a shortcut conflict. Confirm that both the hotkey reference and stored keycode remain absent and that the event tap does not pass an unregistered chord.
8. Verify startup without a usable event tap and normal application termination: no keyboard-lock hotkey should survive without the event tap, and observer, handler, hotkey, and stored-keycode cleanup should remain balanced.

content.text:
# Recommended simplification

Replace the generic keycode scan in [`current_keyboard_lock_key_code`](macos/Lex.swift#L344-L389) with a closed mapping based on the selected input source:

| Input source identifier | Logical “L” position |
|---|---|
| `com.apple.keylayout.ABC` | US ANSI L |
| `com.apple.keylayout.Dvorak` | US ANSI P |

Use the named Carbon constants for those physical positions rather than numeric keycodes.

## Resolution mechanism

1. Query the **selected** source with `TISCopyCurrentKeyboardInputSource`.
2. Read its stable input-source identifier through `kTISPropertyInputSourceID`.
3. Compare it exactly against the ABC and Dvorak identifiers.
4. Return the corresponding US ANSI physical-position keycode.
5. Treat a missing or unknown identifier as resolution failure; do not default to ABC.

`TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource`, currently used at [lines 345–350](macos/Lex.swift#L345-L350), is less appropriate. It identifies the effective translation layout, which can differ from the selected source for input methods. The selected-source API matches the stated contract directly.

## Delete

The resolver no longer needs:

- Unicode keyboard-layout data retrieval.
- Unsafe `UCKeyboardLayout` memory binding.
- The 128-key scan.
- `UCKeyTranslate`.
- Dead-key state and character buffers.
- Keyboard-type and translation-option handling.
- Character-output comparison.

## Retain

Keep the surrounding lifecycle:

- Input-source-change observer.
- Main-queue re-registration.
- Stored registered keycode.
- Event-tap pass-through for the lock/unlock chord.
- Idempotence when the mapped keycode has not changed.
- Hotkey registration failure handling.
- Handler, observer, and hotkey cleanup on termination.

One behavior should be corrected: if source resolution fails, unregister and clear the **previous** hotkey. The current ordering at [lines 289–305](macos/Lex.swift#L289-L305) returns before clearing it, leaving a stale physical shortcut registered after an unsupported source appears.

# Oracle perspective

Oracle agreed this is the smallest sound design under the assumptions and emphasized:

- Use selected-source identity, not effective-layout identity.
- Compare exact reverse-DNS identifiers rather than localized source names.
- Preserve querying inside the queued main-thread registration operation so rapid source changes converge on the latest source.
- Clear the hotkey reference and stored keycode together before changed registration.
- Keep unknown-source recovery possible by retaining the observer and event handler.
- Apple does not expose the ABC and Dvorak identifiers as immutable SDK enum cases, so they should be manually verified on the project’s supported macOS versions.

# Verification

Manual macOS checks should cover:

1. ABC triggers the logical shortcut from the physical ANSI L position.
2. Dvorak triggers it from the physical ANSI P position.
3. Repeated ABC/Dvorak switching updates the shortcut without duplicate registrations.
4. Switching layouts while locked still permits the new logical shortcut to unlock.
5. An unsupported source clears the prior registration and switching back recovers.
6. Registration failure leaves neither a stored keycode nor event-tap pass-through for that chord.

No code or files were changed.
OK. Apply your plan in a simple, minimal way.

I’ll replace only the generic resolver and ensure a failed resolution clears any previously registered physical shortcut. The observer, re-registration lifecycle, and event-tap handling remain unchanged.

# Listener remains compatible

Static tracing confirms the layout-change flow still works:

1. The observer listens for `kTISNotifySelectedKeyboardInputSourceChanged` at [`Lex.swift:279-287`](macos/Lex.swift#L279-L287).

4. Switching ABC ↔ Dvorak changes the resolved keycode, causing the old hotkey to be unregistered and the new one registered at [`Lex.swift:301-327`](macos/Lex.swift#L301-L327).
5. The stored keycode changes with the registration, so event-tap pass-through uses the new physical position.
6. Repeated notifications for the same source are idempotent.
7. Unknown-source resolution clears stale registration; a later ABC/Dvorak notification recovers normally.
8. Termination removes the same observer and unregisters the hotkey.
